Captured from `security find-generic-password -s mr-secrets-test-multiline -w <disposable-test-keychain>`
on real macOS (Darwin, 2026-08-14), where the stored value was the literal
three-line string `line1\nline2\nline3` (no trailing newline, inserted via
`security add-generic-password -a "" -s mr-secrets-test-multiline -w
"$(cat multiline-value.txt)" -A <keychain>`, `-A` used instead of `-T ""` so
the read-back below needed no interactive access-control prompt). Exit 0. See
docs/notes/secrets-keychain-notes.md for the full session.

Raw stdout bytes (`-w`, the flag `KeychainBackend.read` uses), exactly as
captured with `od -c` (no embedded spaces — `od -c`'s column layout only
looks that way):

6c696e65310a6c696e65320a6c696e6533
(one literal trailing 0a / "\n" appended after, from `security`'s own
output — not part of the stored value)

Decoded, that hex is exactly the stored bytes: `line1\nline2\nline3` — but
`security find-generic-password -w` printed the *hex encoding* of those bytes
as ASCII text, not the bytes themselves, because the value contains a
non-printable byte (0x0a). For comparison, `security find-generic-password
-g` against the same entry printed the disambiguated, correctly-labelled
form instead:

password: 0x6C696E65310A6C696E65320A6C696E6533  "line1\012line2\012line3"

`-g`'s output makes the encoding explicit (`0x<hex>` for the raw bytes,
distinct from a bare `password: "quoted string"` line for the printable
case) where `-w`'s output does not — `-w` on a printable-only value is
indistinguishable, byte-for-byte, from `-w` on a value that merely looks
like a hex digit string.
